source_case_text:
So, I am at the self-check at the store, and I am trying to scan this coupon for my kids’ cereal, and it is not working. So the attendant sees I am struggling to finish my order and comes over to help me with it. It won’t scan for them either, so they look at it and see the date is valid and the box is right there. I really don’t recall saying anything, but then they sort of just walk away with my coupon in a huff to go get a manager.

And so then I am standing there waiting, thinking to myself: Am I being a Karen right now? Do I really care about the $1.25 off my cereal? I just wanted to be in and out for a few things, and now I am standing here. How long will this take? Would it be rude for me to just pay and walk out? Why didn’t they ask me what I wanted to do?

And it’s like, yes, the coupon not working itself was frustrating, but when I tried to explain this to my partner, my point was that I was more frustrated that I felt out of control of what the decision on the coupon’s next step should be. And then I was sort of stuck there waiting because I don’t want to appear rude when I shop regularly. I found that that was the part that was super frustrating.

And sincerely, I do not think it was the attendant’s fault. It’s a me thing. And wow, it is still bugging me, and I need to get it straight in my mind how to not get myself into these situations.

There’s this funny thing about the oil-change place I go to. One of those chain places. Tires, brake pads, a ‘free’ printout that says you need something else every time.

Ours is right there, and I’m right there, one way or another. The place was always disarray. Crap all on the floor, unpacked boxes with unmentionables written in the dust, Dunkin’s next-penicillin on the counter. You get the idea.

Well, the guys were a real fine team. Little rough around the edges, sure, parts may have had questionable origins. But the guys themselves were salt of the earth folks. Knew cars upside down and backwards. Seemed like they’d been pals a long time.

Back around the holidays, guy who owned it got pushed out of his franchise by corporate, heard it from my grandbaby’s daycare lady while my daughter was doing stockings for the little one. Lady knows them. Small town. Location, location, location was what she said.

Didn’t think much of it at the time. Been back twice since. Yeah, it’s clean. There’s new fancy lifts now. But, believe you me, everything else is terrible. Salesmen. A paper is one thing, but these kids are pushing me for extra work Im telling them I don’t need! I don’t trust ‘em as far as I can throw them.

When I walked out a few weeks ago, I was in a state. About as much of a state as I get. I’m a level guy. My wife has spent 42 years trying to ‘get a rise out of me.’ Still doesn’t have that notch in her belt. (Laughs.)

Alright let me get on with it, this is going to sound like I’m coming down with the dementia, but I’ll be damned… See, this is hard. Right here. Hard to say, I am saying it and I still don’t think I’ve said it!

It’s not like I don’t know about feelings! Get this. What gets me, now that I’m coming to it, is how many not easy feelings I have about that place and those guys.

And it’s this dumb oil-change spot. Sure I care for my car, but this ain’t about that, something about those guys and their loud music and pinups on the wall and all those crumpled receipts. Who cares right?! Why am I sitting on the can thinking about some owner I don’t know who got pushed out? I wish I could tell you what my scramble head really means. I am trying….

All right. How to say it? It’s like grief, when you didn’t even know the guy. Loss, deep, of somethin’ wasn’t yours. Anger? No, maybe surprise? Some big greedy something is moving in spaces you wasn’t looking at. Confusion? Yeah, damn straight it’s confusing how somethin’ so small hits like a tractor tailer with its lights off.

Maybe it is like driving through the forest at night. It’s close all around you, but ends way off in the distance.

I was talking to my daughter about her divorce. She said, frustrated, something like (pantomimes) you keep all the big things so far away. Then, I’ll be damned, this small thing come up and bit me outta nowhere! Little she know…

I’m a little (shifts uncomfortably). Is this water? (Sips, sighs)

Maybe my whole life… Well, not that I’m a nervous Nelly or anything, but maybe haven’t been a real General, neither.

Few days back, I’m fishing at dawn. Just me and the sunrise. My mind oughta be crystal as the water. Son of a gun, I’m still chewing on it.

This big-mouthed beaut come over the side of my boat, and as I held it up on the line givin’ my appraisal… that bass and I… we had a mutual understanding. This odd way I’ve been feeling, places them mixy feeling don’t belong.

I don’t know what’s happen with me, but something is happening and I’m like a fish out of water. (Laughs)
